messages:
Alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak we pushed yesterday I'm seeing a pronounced tail-latency regression for streaming short responses (1	6 tokens). p95 jumped ~45ms -> ~120ms on small kernels.
Maya: gah. link to the perf dash? anything in traces?
Alex: Perf dash: https://perf.redwood/internal/dash/streaming-tiny. Traces show extra time in "coalesce_wait" and "kernel_setup" for these flows.
Sam: can you repro locally with loadgen? logs?
Alex: repro with local loadgen (small-chat profile). Command I used:
```
./run_loadgen --profile small-chat --concurrency 16 --stream
```
Sample output (times in ms):
- coalesce_wait: 3.2
- kernel_setup: 1.9
- partial_decode_wait: 2.7
Total per-response tail increases match dash.
Priya: did you check KV cache hit rates? if KV warmup is worse we'll see more setup on tiny streams.
Alex: KV hit rate dropped ~12% for the streaming route after selector change. Prefetch probe shows more cold misses on initial tokens.
Noah: remind me what the selector change did? I thought we only changed throughput weighting.
Alex: we switched to prefer kernels by throughput_per_batch metric (improves heavy-batch throughput). Side-effect: for batch_size=1/2 kernels with higher constant setup get picked because their steady throughput wins the metric.
Maya: that explains it — those kernels have higher amortized startup but better steady throughput.
Sam: coalesce window also changed in the same deploy, right? from 1ms -> 3ms for general workloads.
Alex: correct. combined effect: longer coalesce + a kernel with ~2ms setup = visible latency hit on tiny streams.
Priya: partial-decode scheduling looks affected too — telemetry shows partial-decode queue waits spike in line with coalesce window. Log snippet:
"partial-decode-await=3.1ms kernel-init=1.8ms kv-prefetch=2.2ms"
Noah: quick mitigation idea: bias kernel selection for streaming routes to latency-first, or add a token_budget_target that penalizes kernels with setup > threshold.
Alex: proposed config patch for streaming route:
```
routes:
  streaming:
    token_budget_target: 8
    kernel_preference: latency_first
```
This keeps token budget small so selector prefers low-setup kernels and avoids large coalesce windows.
Maya: can we instead scope coalesce window down for streaming route only? e.g., 1ms for streaming, 3ms default.
Sam: yes we have route-level coalesce settings — that'll be faster to toggle. Also want a telemetry guard: emit kernel_setup_ms per kernel+route so selector can learn.
Priya: agree on kernel_setup_ms metric. also add kv-hit-rate per route to the perf dashboard so we can correlate.
Ops-bot: deploy bot: Canary deploy started for service/runtime-kernel-picker v2 — canary id c-20260317-17
Alex: I'll roll a canary that flips kernel_preference -> latency_first and sets token_budget_target=6 for the streaming route, plus route-scoped coalesce=1ms. Running A/B with k6 small-chat to measure.
Noah: add a threshold in selector: if kernel_setup_ms > token_budget_target_ms then deprioritize, so we don't pick high-setup kernels for small token budgets.
Maya: also run microbench with kernels pinned to quantify tradeoffs (throughput vs setup). Test matrix: batch sizes [1,2,4,8], seq len [8,32,64], kernels pinned.
Sam: PR please with config + telemetry. put canary id in PR description. Also include rollback steps (how to revert route override quickly).
Alex: PR #4821 created — flips streaming route preference + adds kernel_setup telemetry. K6 runs queued.
Priya: once canary results look good, we should bake new selector policy but keep old behavior behind a feature flag for a week.
Maya: :thumbsup: keep me posted, I'll help with dashboard panels and trace links.
Alex: will post k6 numbers and traces here in ~30m. If canary shows no regression we'll promote, else rollback plan ready.
